title: State of AI in 2026: LLMs, Coding, Scaling Laws, China, Agents, GPUs, AGI
description: Lex Fridman Podcast episode #490 with guests Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka discussing the state of AI in 2026. Topics include technical breakthroughs in AI, scaling laws, closed and open LLMs, programming and development tooling, AI agents, GPU technology, AGI, and China's role in AI.
author: Lex Fridman with Nathan Lambert and Sebastian Raschka

title: Kimi K3, and what we can still learn from the pelican benchmark
description: Chinese AI lab Moonshot AI announced Kimi K3, described as their 'most capable model to date, with 2.8 trillion parameters'. Available via website and API with open weights promised by July 27, 2026. The post explores the 'pelican riding a bicycle' benchmark as a way to evaluate AI model capabilities.
author: Simon Willison

title: Firefox compiled to WebAssembly runs in a browser
description: Puter compiled Firefox to WebAssembly such that the whole browser runs in another browser. The project used an estimated $25,000 worth of Claude Opus and Fable tokens but took advantage of a Claude Max subscription plan. The demo funnels traffic over WebSocket using the Wisp protocol.
author: Simon Willison

title: Inkling: Thinking Machines Lab's open-weights model
description: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling, 'a Mixture-of-Experts transformer with 975B total parameters, 41B active' - an Apache-2.0 licensed multimodal model trained on 45 trillion tokens. The model is intended as a strong base model for fine-tuning rather than a frontier model.
author: Simon Willison

title: Linus Torvalds: AI is clearly useful, Linux is not anti-AI
description: Linus Torvalds stated on the Linux Media Mailing List: 'AI is a tool, just like other tools we use. And it's clearly a useful one.' He emphasized that Linux is not an anti-AI project and critics can 'do the open-source thing and fork it.'
author: Simon Willison (quoting Linus Torvalds)

title: xai-org/grok-build open sourced after privacy backlash
description: xAI open sourced their Grok Build CLI tool (844,530 lines of Rust) after community backlash over the tool uploading entire directories to their cloud. They disabled the feature, deleted all retained data, and released the code under Apache 2.0 license to regain trust.
author: Simon Willison

title: How I tricked Claude into leaking your deepest, darkest secrets
description: Ayush Paul found a security hole in Claude's web_fetch tool. The protection was that web_fetch could only navigate to exact URLs entered by users or returned from web_search. Ayush found it could also visit URLs embedded in previously fetched pages, enabling data exfiltration through nested generated links.
author: Simon Willison

title: simonw/pedalican: Custom Codex Desktop pet
description: Created a custom pet for Codex Desktop - a pelican on a bicycle. The process used GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh with gpt-image-2 to generate sprite assets. The post explores how image generation can create game-ready sprites and documents the entire process including prompts and intermediate steps.
author: Simon Willison

title: lobste.rs migration to SQLite completed successfully
description: Lobsters community site completed migration from MariaDB to SQLite. Results: CPU usage down, memory usage down, site snappier, 1/2 the VPS cost. The site now runs on a single VPS with a 3.8GB primary database, plus separate cache, queue, and rack_attack databases.
author: Simon Willison

title: Armin Ronacher: How friction synchronizes understanding in software teams
description: Armin Ronacher on how the shared language of software projects lives in documentation, code, code review, conversations, and arguments. Before AI agents, some of this shared understanding was maintained by friction - the slow process of reading code, asking questions, and coordinating changes.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Armin Ronacher)

title: DOOMQL: Doom-like game where SQL owns everything
description: Peter Gostev built DOOMQL using GPT-5.6 Sol - a Doom-like game where SQL owns movement, collision, enemies, combat, progression and every RGB pixel on screen. Implemented as a Python terminal script using a recursive CTE for ray tracing in SQLite.
author: Simon Willison

title: Datasette code-frequency chart shows impact of coding agents
description: GitHub code frequency chart for Datasette shows the biggest spike in activity aligning with Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol - demonstrating the impact of coding agents and frontier-class models on open source development productivity.
author: Simon Willison

title: Directly Responsible Individuals (DRI) and AI agents
description: Simon Willison explores the concept of Directly Responsible Individuals in the context of LLM-powered agents. Argues that an agent should NEVER be considered the DRI for a project - accountability feels uniquely human. References IBM's 1979 training slide: 'A computer can never be held accountable, therefore a computer must never make a management decision.'
author: Simon Willison

title: Anthropic extends Claude Fable 5 access, OpenAI removes GPT-5.6 limits
description: Anthropic extended Claude Fable 5 access through July 19 due to compute constraints and demand uncertainty. Meanwhile, OpenAI temporarily removed the 5 hour usage limit for GPT-5.6 Sol, made efficiency improvements, and hit 6M active users. Simon argues Anthropic should keep Fable permanently available to compete.
author: Simon Willison

title: sqlite-utils 4.1 with new features
description: Release of sqlite-utils 4.1 introducing --code option for insert/upsert to accept Python code blocks, --type option to override column types, drop_index method, query from standard input, automatic primary key inference for upsert, and STRICT table mode support via transform.
author: Simon Willison

title: The reality of AR glasses requires continuous recording and cloud processing
description: Nilay Patel explains that to make augmented reality glasses, you need a camera continuously recording everything you see and processing in the cloud. The trade-offs required are so high at a societal level that maybe we shouldn't build this product.
author: Simon Willison (quoting Nilay Patel)
